Top News
 
 
 
 Fed decision, Microsoft and Alphabet earnings highlight blockbuster week 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 Wall Street heads into a packed week with a Federal Reserve interest-rate decision and earnings from several of the world’s largest technology companies likely to set the tone for markets.

 The Fed takes center stage Wednesday, with policymakers announcing their decision at 2 p.m. ET, followed by Chairman Kevin Warsh’s press conference. Federal funds futures imply only about a 10% chance of another 25-basis-point rate increase. Investors will then turn to Thursday’s first estimate of third-quarter GDP and the October core PCE price index, with economists forecasting annualized GDP growth of 3.0%.

 Earnings will provide an equally important test. Alphabet ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) report Wednesday, followed by Amazon ( AMZN ) Thursday, putting AI spending, cloud growth and the return on massive data center investments back in focus.

 Microsoft’s report could draw particular attention as investors weigh strong Azure demand against rising capital spending and questions over AI returns. Seeking Alpha analysts currently span the spectrum from Strong Buy to Hold to Sell on the stock.

 Elsewhere, Apple ( AAPL ) will hold a product event Wednesday, while Oracle’s ( ORCL ) AI World conference begins Sunday in Las Vegas.


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Earnings
 
 
 
 Earnings spotlight: Monday, Oct. 26: Verizon ( VZ ), Welltower ( WELL ), Nucor ( NUE ), Public Storage ( PSA ). See the full earnings calendar .

 Earnings spotlight: Tuesday, Oct. 27: Visa ( V ), Coca-Cola ( KO ), Boeing ( BA ), UPS ( UPS ), S&P Global ( SPGI ). See the full earnings calendar .

 Earnings spotlight : Wednesday, Oct. 28: Alphabet ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), T-Mobile US ( TMUS ), Chipotle ( CMG ), eBay ( EBAY ), GE Vernova ( GEV ). See the full earnings calendar .

 Earnings spotlight : Thursday, Oct. 29: Amazon ( AMZN ), Eli Lilly ( LLY ), Mastercard ( MA ), Intel ( INTC ), Merck ( MRK ), Caterpillar ( CAT ), Shell ( SHEL ). See the full earnings calendar .

 Earnings spotlight : Friday, Oct. 30: ExxonMobil ( XOM ), Chevron ( CVX ), BP ( BP ), AbbVie ( ABBV ). See the full earnings calendar .

Analysis
 
 
 
 Investing Group Spotlight 
 
 
With AI-driven growth reshaping markets, investors face a challenging balance between identifying opportunities and managing risks. While strong earnings and profitability support the current rally, questions remain about the sustainability of massive AI investments. In the following article, Leo Nelissen highlights three stocks worth watching: Amazon, Ares Management, and Miami International Holdings, each offering distinct growth opportunities, valuations, and risks in today's evolving market environment.

( Free Full Article ) Here’s a brief summary of the article:

The current market rally is supported by strong corporate profitability and earnings growth, making leading stocks relatively more attractive despite elevated AI valuations. However, its sustainability depends on whether massive AI investments translate into lasting productivity gains and profitable applications. Leo favors selective stock picking over broad market exposure amid these uncertainties.

Amazon ( AMZN ) offers long-term growth potential through AWS, its expanding semiconductor business, diversified operations, and substantial AI demand. Despite negative free cash flow driven by aggressive capital expenditure, its growing backlog supports the investment thesis. Ares Management ( ARES ) benefits from expanding private credit demand, substantial assets under management, and attractive growth prospects, although a recession or disappointing AI returns could hurt credit quality and demand.

Miami International Holdings ( MIAX ) presents a higher-risk opportunity through exchange industry disruption, new products, and a strong balance sheet. However, declining options volumes, falling market share, and execution challenges remain concerns. Overall, the author remains bullish on all three companies, emphasizing their valuations and long-term potential while recognizing that AI investment returns, economic conditions, and execution will determine their performance.
